_説明: Explanations shown when you click a word in the code (English). tools/make_glossaries.py makes this file from the dictionaries in tools/glossary/en/ (fix the dictionaries, not this file).
$ docker: The Docker command. Handles containers and images
$ docker run: Makes a container from an image and runs it
$ docker --rm: Deletes the container automatically when it stops
$ docker -d: Runs in the background (gives the terminal back)
$ docker --env-file: Reads environment variables from a file
$ docker -v: Connects a folder or volume into the container (-v outside:inside)
$ docker -it: Lets you operate it from the keyboard (-i takes input, -t uses a terminal)
$ docker -t: In docker build, the image's name (tag); in docker run, use a terminal
$ docker -w: The working folder inside the container
$ docker --user: The user to run as inside the container
$ docker --privileged: Lets the container use all the computer's devices (dangerous; only when needed)
$ docker --platform: The kind of CPU (linux/arm64 and so on)
$ docker build: Makes an image from a Dockerfile
$ docker image: Handles images (ls, rm, prune and so on)
$ docker container: Handles containers (ls, rm, prune and so on)
$ docker ps: The list of running containers. -a includes stopped ones
$ docker -f: Forces it (stops and deletes even if running, and so on)
$ docker exec: Runs a command inside a running container
$ docker system: Handles Docker as a whole (df shows space used, prune cleans up)
$ docker login: Logs in to Docker Hub or the like
$ docker push: Uploads an image to Docker Hub or the like
$ docker pull: Fetches an image from Docker Hub or the like
$ docker compose: Runs the containers written in compose.yaml together
$ docker compose up: Starts them together. -d in the background, --build rebuilds first
$ docker buildx: A newer build tool that can make images for many kinds of CPU
$ docker --push: Uploads the built image right away
$ docker --install: Uses buildx as the normal docker build
$ get-docker.sh: The official script that installs Docker
FROM: The image to start from (written first in a Dockerfile)
WORKDIR: The working folder inside the container (made if missing)
COPY: Copies files from the computer into the image
RUN: Runs a command while building the image (installing software and so on)
EXPOSE: A note of the port the container uses (-p is what actually connects it)
CMD: The command run when the container starts
slim: A small image cut down to only what is needed
services: In compose.yaml, the list of containers to run
build: In compose.yaml, where the Dockerfile is (builds the image)
image: In compose.yaml, the image to use
ports: In compose.yaml, how ports are connected ("computer:container")
volumes: In compose.yaml, how volumes and folders are connected
depends_on: In compose.yaml, containers to start first
command: In compose.yaml, the command to start (instead of the Dockerfile's CMD)
redis: A fast database that keeps values in memory
incr: Adds 1 to a value in Redis
flask: A small web framework for Python
route: Says "when this URL is requested, call the function below"
run.host: "0.0.0.0" makes it reachable from outside the container too
run.debug: True shows errors in detail and reloads automatically after changes
requirements: The file listing the Python libraries used (requirements.txt)
dockerignore: The list of files not put in the image (.dockerignore)
TZ: The time zone (Asia/Tokyo and so on)
import: Loads a module (another file or library). You can give it a short name with as, as in import numpy as np
from: Loads only part of a module. from datetime import date
def: Makes a function. After def name(arguments):, write the body indented
return: Returns the function's answer and ends the function
__name__: The current file's name. It is '__main__' only when the file is run directly
if: Runs only when the condition is true
for: Takes the contents of a container one at a time and repeats
while: Repeats while the condition is true
in: In for, "one at a time from..."; in a condition, "whether it is in..."
is: Whether two things are the same object. Used to check for None, as in x is None
open: Opens a file. "r" reads, "w" writes (overwrites), "a" appends
get: Gets a value from a dictionary. If the key is missing, returns None (or the second argument)
format: Puts values into a string (f"..." f-strings do the same)
os: A module for handling the OS (files, folders, environment variables)
environ: A dictionary of environment variables. os.environ.get("NAME", default)
json: A module for reading and writing JSON files
venv: A Python virtual environment (a per-project place for libraries)
pip: The tool for installing Python libraries
$ sudo:
Origin: short for superuser do (run as the administrator).
Runs the following command with administrator rights. Needed to change system settings or install software.
It asks for your password the first time (nothing appears on screen as you type).
$ apt:
Origin: short for Advanced Package Tool.
The command that manages software on Ubuntu. It installs and removes software.
$ apt install:
Installs software from the internet.
Example: sudo apt install pipx installs pipx.
$ ls:
Origin: short for list.
Shows a list of files and folders.
$ cd:
Origin: short for change directory.
Moves to another folder in the terminal.
$ cat:
Origin: short for concatenate (join together).
Shows the contents of a file.
$ ssh-add: Adds a key to ssh-agent (the helper that remembers keys). Once added, you do not have to type the passphrase every time.
$ ssh-add -l:
Origin: -l is short for list.
Shows the list of keys ssh-agent remembers.
$ exit: When you are logged in with ssh, logs out and returns to the original machine.
$ git: Software that records changes to source code. It keeps track of when and what changed, lets you go back to an earlier state, and lets you put code on GitHub.
$ git push: Sends (uploads) your local commits to GitHub.
$ git pull: Brings new commits on GitHub into your local repository. Used to get changes made on another PC.
$ git tag:
Origin: a tag is a label, like one tied to luggage.
Puts a named marker such as v1.0.0 on the current commit. Lets you find and take out a version you shipped later.
$ git --version: Shows git's version. If it shows one, git is installed.
$ git rm:
Origin: rm is short for remove.
Deletes a file and puts that deletion into the next commit.
$ git rm -r:
Origin: -r is short for recursive (everything inside, too).
Applies to everything inside the folder.
$ code:
The command that starts VS Code from the terminal.
code collar opens the collar folder in VS Code. code . opens the current folder.
$ .gitignore: A file listing the files git should not record. One per line: folders like build/, or patterns like *.csv. Everything after # is a note.
Opens the current folder in VS Code.
$ apt update: Refreshes the list of software (which versions are available). Do it before apt install
$ ls -l: Lists files in detail (permissions, size, date and time)
Loads a settings file into the current terminal (the same as source)
$ :: A leading : means "a file on the Pico". Without :, it is a file on the PC.
$ grep:
Origin: short for global regular expression print.
Picks out only the lines that contain some text.
Example: | grep 2e8a keeps only the lines containing 2e8a.
$ |:
Origin: a pipe, like data flowing through a pipe.
Passes the result of the command on the left to the command on the right.
$ rm:
Origin: short for remove.
Deletes a file. It does not go to the trash and cannot be undone.
$ hello.py: A file on the PC with the code you want to run. You choose the name.
$ echo:
Origin: an echo.
Outputs the text you write as it is.
$ rm -f:
Origin: -f is short for force.
Deletes without an error even if the file is missing, and without asking.
$ mkdir:
Origin: short for make directory.
Makes a folder.
$ mkdir -p:
Origin: -p is short for parents.
Also makes the folders along the way. No error if it already exists.
$ pwd:
Origin: short for print working directory.
Shows the folder you are in, in the terminal.
$ systemctl:
Origin: short for system control.
The command that manages Linux services. The Pico does not have it.
$ systemctl enable: Sets a service to start automatically at boot.
$ systemctl restart: Stops a service and starts it again.
$ sh:
Origin: short for shell.
Runs a shell script.
$ pip:
Origin: said to be short for pip installs packages.
Installs Python libraries. It cannot be used on the Pico.
$ bash: Starts the shell (bash). -c runs the following string as a command
$ curl: Downloads data from a URL (also used to call web APIs)
$ curl -o: Sets the file name to save to
$ curl -fsSL: A shorthand for stop on errors, quiet, and follow redirects
$ usermod -aG: Adds the user to a group (-a adds, -G is group). Takes effect after logging in again
$ python: Runs Python (the same as python3 inside a virtual environment)
